# Independent audit of all-status anchored residual credit

Full independent read of `candidate 6d98cff7cbcfe25c`: **PASS**.

The split at total endpoint capture B>=min V_j correctly handles every full-source capture without inserting an empty residual into Brunn--Minkowski. In the other branch every residual has positive full-dimensional volume. Their strict halfspace inequalities are preserved by the actual positive barycentric relation. Their closures give the same volumes, so the compact-body BM inequality applies; a zero continuous normal is separately valid because every positive residual is the entire fiber. The inverse credit uses increasing convex root-depletion functions and an exact simplex allocation bound, with the strict positive residual root ensuring that the inverse is taken on its unsaturated branch. The scalar equality construction is correctly described only as equality for these numerical alternatives, not as geometric realizability.

The multiple-relation allocation counts each actual captured fiber at most once and uses one fixed actual anchor. Its finite allocation polytope is compact, since every hyperedge is nonempty and forces its own coefficient at most one. There is no implicit coverage or existence claim for enough useful relations.

For the thirteen-volume application, the actual ternary relation and all three positive residual lower bounds are valid whenever their total captured mass is at most 1/100. The printed exact rational product gap and the elementary Gamma_d>4/11 proof give a contradiction in every d>=1. The conclusion takes the infimum correctly: the uniform own-fiber bound plus the constant 1/100 yields the fixed margin at least 3/1300. Closed boundaries and purely integer halfspaces remain covered by the first theorem.

Reran `supporting computation verify_all_status_anchored_residual_payment_slab_recovery.py`: 208 exact checks plus the inherited 2,112 quota checks pass. No correction is required. This is an all-shape payment for the specified volume vector, not a general theorem that every complete lattice base or admissible quota vector has a paying anchored relation.
